questions.explanation: Different test levels catch different failures. Unit tests are fast; integration/e2e tests cover wiring and workflows.

concept_panel.title: Testing Scope
concept_panel.explanation: Different tests answer different questions. Unit tests verify small logic in isolation; integration tests verify boundaries such as API plus database; end-to-end tests verify user workflows. Good test strategy uses the cheapest test that catches the failure mode. Coverage is useful, but meaningful assertions matter more than line counts.
key_takeaways: Unit tests are fast and narrow.
Integration tests verify real boundaries.
Coverage does not prove correctness by itself.
concept_panel.interview_insight: Interviewers usually ask this concept to evaluate whether you can choose tests based on risk and feedback speed.
concept_panel.practical_example: A pure XP formula should be unit-tested; an API route writing to SQLite deserves an integration test.

questions.prompt: What should CI run before merge?
questions.explanation: CI should automatically run the checks that protect code quality before changes merge.

concept_panel.title: CI/CD Pipelines
concept_panel.explanation: CI validates changes automatically with tests, type checks, and builds. CD deploys a validated artifact to an environment. The important principle is that the artifact you deploy should be traceable to the code that passed checks. Deployment health checks and rollbacks limit blast radius when a bad version escapes.
key_takeaways: CI catches broken changes before merge/deploy.
CD should deploy a known artifact.
Health checks and rollback make releases safer.
concept_panel.interview_insight: Interviewers usually ask this concept to evaluate whether you understand deployment safety and operational traceability.
concept_panel.practical_example: A pipeline installs dependencies, runs tests, builds an artifact, then deploys it with health checks.

questions.prompt: Two services must agree on request/response shape. What catches drift?

questions.explanation: Coverage shows executed lines, not whether tests assert the right behavior.
options: Coverage is not proof of meaningful tests
Coverage means all bugs are impossible
questions.answer: Coverage is not proof of meaningful tests

coding_challenges.title: Quality and Testing status classifier
coding_challenges.instructions: Implement classify_status_code(code: int) -> str. Return success for 200-299, redirect for 300-399, client_error for 400-499, server_error for 500-599, and unknown otherwise.
coding_challenges.explanation: The challenge reinforces deterministic branching, status-code categories, and local test execution.
